data.long_meaning: The name Sathyam is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Satya', which means truth. It is a unisex name, popular in Hindu communities, and is considered auspicious and sacred. The name represents the qualities of honesty, goodness, and morality. The name Sathyam carries the meaning “Truth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Tamil, Sanskrit, Malayalam. Parents who choose Sathyam usually hope their child will grow to embody truth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It reminds us of the importance of being truthful in all aspects of life, not just to others but also to ourselves. The name Sathyam thus serves as a constant reminder of the importance of truth and the inner peace that comes with living a truthful life.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu god Sathyam, also known as Satyam or Satyavacaspati, is a form of Lord Vishnu who embodies truth and righteousness. He is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Sanskrit epic, as a form of Vishnu that is often invoked for truth and justice in legal matters.

Another reference to Sathyam can be found in the Puranic texts, specifically in the Skanda Purana. In this text, Sathyam is described as the divine messenger of Lord Vishnu, charged with maintaining truth and righteousness in the universe.
